get.description:
The job.

`queued`, `parsing`, `parsed`, and `extracting` are `job_id` and `status`. `failed`
adds `error`. `done` adds the ETS rows. Open and failed jobs do not read the
extraction artifact.

`?detail=full` adds the stored record: `created_at`, `display_name`, `parser`,
`extractor`, and `document_checksum`. A done job then also adds each row's observation
index.

AcceptedJobResponse.title: AcceptedJobResponse
AcceptedJobResponse.description: The 202 body from queueing a job. A later read carries the stored record.

BoundingBox.title: BoundingBox
BoundingBox.description: Axis-aligned box in page space, top-left origin, normalized to [0, 1].

CategoricalTrait.title: CategoricalTrait
CategoricalTrait.description: One of a closed set of levels. It has no unit.

Citation.title: Citation
Citation.description:
Printed text. On a citation-only column, this text is the ETS value.

A range list, when present, concatenates to ``text``.

Correction.title: Correction
Correction.description:
A narrow citation kept beside an interpretation.

``citation`` is the narrow printed token. The interpretation's passage is
the wider text its value was read from.

CountTrait.title: CountTrait
CountTrait.description:
A number of things, such as young or teats.

It is never converted, so the printed unit is not checked. It is a whole number, unless
the paper prints a mean or a median of counts. ``stored_unit`` names what is counted.

DoneJobFullResponse.title: DoneJobFullResponse
DoneJobFullResponse.description: A finished job with the record and the observation index.

DoneJobResponse.title: DoneJobResponse
DoneJobResponse.description: A finished job: the ETS rows built from its extraction artifact.

EtsRow.title: EtsRow
EtsRow.description:
ETS v0.10 core, taxon, measurement-or-fact, and occurrence columns.

The order follows the stored observation. Columns the artifact does not
store sit beside the field they belong with.

EtsSourceRow.title: EtsSourceRow
EtsSourceRow.description:
An ETS row plus the observation it was built from.

``source_index`` is not an ETS column. It is the position in the artifact's
observations, so a row can be matched back to the observation that produced it.

ExtractionArtifact.title: ExtractionArtifact
ExtractionArtifact.description: Versioned extraction result stored for a job.

FailedJobFullResponse.title: FailedJobFullResponse
FailedJobFullResponse.description: A failed job with the stored record beside the error.

Interpretation.title: Interpretation
Interpretation.description: A value read from one citation. ``passage`` is that citation.

ListedJobFullResponse.title: ListedJobFullResponse
ListedJobFullResponse.description: One listed job with the stored record. Still no ETS rows.

ListedJobResponse.title: ListedJobResponse
ListedJobResponse.description: One job in a list. A done job does not include its ETS rows.

NumericTrait.title: NumericTrait
NumericTrait.description: A measured quantity. Each printed unit maps to the factor into ``stored_unit``.

Observation.title: Observation
Observation.description:
One measurement.

A citation-only field is the printed token. A citation or correction is that
token, or the token kept beside a reading of a wider phrase. A citation or
interpretation is the printed token, or a value read from a wider phrase.
``basisOfRecord`` and ``aggregateMeasure`` are interpretations only. A paper
does not print those tokens.

The minimum, the maximum, and the dispersion are the numbers the paper
printed, read with ``verbatimTraitUnit``. ``statisticalMethod`` is the
phrase the paper printed, or empty.

``scientificName``, ``traitValue``, and ``traitUnit`` are interpretations
beside a verbatim citation. The interpretation is omitted when the printed
token is already the value. They stay empty until a taxonomy lookup or a
trait list standardizes them. ``scientificName`` is another name a later
taxonomy lookup can try.

The artifact does not enforce a closed set of values. An interpretation's
``value`` is any non-empty string, including ``traitCode``. An extractor may
constrain it, and the adapter decides what a value means.

Every other column a paper can state is optional. An extractor leaves it null.

OpenJobFullResponse.title: OpenJobFullResponse
OpenJobFullResponse.description: An open job with the stored record beside the status.

OpenJobResponse.title: OpenJobResponse
OpenJobResponse.description: A job that is not done and has not failed. It has no observations.

SafeError.title: SafeError
SafeError.description: A short, non-sensitive description of why a job failed.

TextRange.title: TextRange
TextRange.description:
Half-open character range in one parser block.

``start`` and ``end`` are Unicode code points, the same indexes as a Python
``str``. ``end`` is greater than ``start``.

TextSpan.title: TextSpan
TextSpan.description: Word box mapped onto `TextContent.text` as a half-open character range.

TraitListEts.title: TraitListEts
TraitListEts.description: The trait list as ETS Traitlist rows, plus the list version.

version.title: Version
version.description: YYYY.MM.REVISION. The year and month the release was made, then a revision that starts at 0 and counts further releases in that month.

TraitListFull.title: TraitListFull
TraitListFull.description:
Full entries for one query.

This is not a closed list. A deprecated trait's replacement may sit outside
the selection, so it is not required to be one of these traits.

TraitlistRow.title: TraitlistRow
TraitlistRow.description: One ETS v0.10 Traitlist row. Empty columns are null.
